engine: This is the briefing engine, demonstrated on Astrotech's public record. The internal version, on Outlook, SharePoint and OneDrive, remains to be built.
headline: One subject followed across three filings, then the five things that moved since the briefing of August 31. Everything else keeps its state and is listed at the foot without being repeated.
scope: Built from the public record alone: filings accepted by EDGAR, press releases, and the company's own pages, read on September 15, 2026. No internal source of any kind.

tracked.subject: The at-the-market equity program

lines.label: AS IT STOOD BEFORE
lines.text: An offering agreement signed on June 2, 2026 with H.C. Wainwright & Co., LLC as sales agent, and a prospectus supplement dated June 3, 2026 covering up to approximately $24.5 million of common stock.

lines.label: WHAT CHANGED
lines.text: On August 19, 2026, accepted at 17:26 Eastern, a prospectus supplement covering up to $50 million replaces and supersedes the June one. A second supplement filed the same minute terminates the June offering, and no further sales may be made under it.

lines.label: WHAT WAS ALREADY DONE
lines.text: 258,856 shares had been sold under the June supplement for gross proceeds of approximately $7.9 million as of August 19, 2026.

lines.label: WHY IT IS RAISED
lines.text: A replacement, not an addition: the two amounts are not added, and the June supplement no longer describes anything. An amount registered is capacity to sell, not capital raised. Any internal document, model or board page that still points at the June program is describing something that has been shut.

tracked.unknown: Whether any shares have been sold under the August supplement, and how many. The public record does not say, and this briefing does not estimate it.

items.headline: The window to nominate a director for the 2026 annual meeting shut on Sunday

what_happened.text: The bylaw window for stockholder proposals and director nominations at the 2026 annual meeting shut at the close of business on Sunday, September 13. It opened on August 14.

what_changed.text: At the previous briefing it was open with thirteen days to run. It is shut.

why_it_matters.text: The same paragraph reopens it for ten days after a public announcement if the 2026 meeting falls more than 30 days before, or more than 60 days after, December 12. The public record does not state the date of the 2026 meeting, so whether the window stays shut is not settled by these sources.

who_owns_it.text: The bylaws name the Secretary of the Company as the recipient. Scott Bartley has held that office, with Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, since October 27, 2025.

decision_required.text: No outstanding decision established from these sources. What the record shows is a window that has shut and a meeting date that has not been published.

items.headline: The annual report for the year ended June 30 is due in thirteen days, on Monday September 28

what_happened.text: The fiscal year ended June 30. The company reports as a non-accelerated filer and a smaller reporting company, which puts the annual report ninety days after the year end: Monday, September 28.

what_changed.text: Twenty eight days remained at the previous briefing. Thirteen remain.

who_owns_it.text: Not designated in public sources. Recent filings are signed by Thomas B. Pickens III as Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer, and RBSM LLP was ratified by stockholders as auditor for this fiscal year.

what_is_late.text: Nothing. The deadline is ahead. Last year the annual report was filed on the eighty eighth day, one day after the results release.

items.headline: Seven amended insider reports were filed in thirteen minutes on September 8, one correcting a report from March 2024
answers: WHAT CHANGED IN THE LAST 24 HOURS

what_happened.text: EDGAR indexes seven Forms 4/A under September 8, accepted between 21:02 and 21:15 Eastern, amending reports for five insiders. One corrects a report originally filed on March 18, 2024.

what_changed.text: None of it existed at the previous briefing. One amended report was a week old: the Form 4 filed September 1 carries a date of earliest transaction of December 13, 2024 while the award it reports is dated September 1, 2026, and the amendment restates that date.

why_it_matters.text: This is the material from which one paragraph of the next proxy statement is drafted: the company has to name any insider whose Section 16(a) report was filed late during the fiscal year, and last year's proxy named three. The filings are visible here; what prompted them is not, and this briefing does not guess at it.

who_owns_it.text: Not stated in public sources. Four of the five are directors and the fifth is the Chief Operating Officer.

items.new_since_previous: the company's board page was read on September 15, sixty one days after the seventh director was appointed
items.headline: Two public statements of the board's size, in the same filing, do not match
answers: WHAT SHOULD I KNOW THAT NOBODY HAS DIRECTLY TOLD ME

what_happened.text: Item 5.02 of the Form 8-K of July 22 says the Board went from six directors to seven. The press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to that same filing says five to six.

what_changed.text: The Executive Team page, read on September 15, presents the Chairman and five directors, six names, sixty one days after the July 16 board action. It lists no Chief Financial Officer, while an Interim Chief Financial Officer has been in office since October 27, 2025.

why_it_matters.text: Six directors stood for election on December 12, 2025, so the Item 5.02 figure is the one that agrees with the rest of the record. The 2026 proxy statement will state one number.

items.new_since_previous: the expiration is now inside the horizon this briefing reports on
items.headline: The rights plan reaches its Final Expiration Date on December 20

what_happened.text: Amendment No. 3, entered into December 12, 2025, extends the Final Expiration Date to 5:00 P.M. New York City time on December 20, 2026. Ninety six days out.

what_changed.text: Nothing about the agreement. It is repeated because its date has come inside the horizon this briefing reports on.

why_it_matters.text: The three amendments were signed December 18, 2023, December 12, 2024 and December 12, 2025. The annual meetings of those years fell on December 15, December 13 and December 12, so each amendment landed within three days of its meeting. That is a pattern in the record, not a commitment.

who_owns_it.text: The agreement is between the Company and Equiniti Trust Company as rights agent.

decision_required.text: No outstanding decision established from these sources. The date is in the record; what happens at it is not.

alert_rule.rule: Three or more amended insider reports accepted inside one hour.
alert_rule.caveat: An illustrative rule, written for this sample. Nothing here has been approved by anyone at Astrotech.

crosses.text: Seven Forms 4/A for five insiders, accepted in thirteen minutes. Three would have been enough; seven is not a clerical slip in one report.

does_not_cross.text: The press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to the June 16 Form 8-K carries the same event as the filing it is attached to. One event, one alert. Republishing a document, or the same news arriving by a second route, fires nothing.

alert_rule.production: A rule worth switching on weighs three things this one ignores: how urgent it is, whether the Chairman's own intervention is needed, and whether the matter has already reached him. A decision he took himself before it was published is not an alert.

carried.text: The board approved a sale process for 1st Detect on June 16. The record does not say it has been signed, priced or dated, and nothing since adds to it.
A Phase 1 proposal to the NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services 2 program was submitted on June 30. No decision date is stated.

The quarterly report for the period ended March 31 was amended on August 6. The amendment states one correction, the Series D conversion share count, and this briefing republishes none of the quarter's figures as news.
Matthew Kreps joined the board on July 16 and had not been assigned to a committee as of July 22.
